4f7375de54a6575b57169521e99b23235d4fd7d0 hw/riscv/andes_ae350: honor -object memory-backend-file for DRAM
Adopt the modern machine->ram idiom used by virt.c and most other QEMU
machines: set mc->default_ram_id and let the machine framework either
auto-create an anonymous memory-backend (the existing behavior) or
consume a user-supplied -object memory-backend-file,id=mem (the new
capability). Replace the local memory_region_init_ram(main_mem, ...)
+ add_subregion(..., main_mem) pair with a single add_subregion that
binds the DRAM range to machine->ram.

Behavior is unchanged for users who do not pass -object memory-backend:
the framework auto-creates an anonymous backend with the default_ram_id,
identical to the prior init_ram call. Users who pass
-machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem now get DRAM backed by a shared
file - required for the hybrid-sim QEMU<->vsim shared-RAM round-trip on
this board.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

f98ca9b62492845ce3d06fd5f9c3a3480a81e390 behavioral: add debugger write support for vl/vtype CSRs
vl (CSR 0xC20) and vtype (CSR 0xC21) are architecturally read-only
CSRs -- the spec only allows setting them via vsetvl/vsetvli.
The gdbstub handback path needs to restore saved values via P-packets
(for the hybrid QEMU->vsim->QEMU2 round-trip).

Two changes:
- write_vl / write_vtype: direct env->vl / env->vtype writes, with
  vill extracted from the MSB of the packed vtype representation.
- riscv_csrrw_check: skip the read-only gate when env->debugger is
  set (same flag already used for other debug-mode CSR overrides).

21587eb0bde1031af35c8cfe5bea03f09e6e39c2 scripts/hotloops: add baremetal support, RVV filter, LLM report, and docs
Extend the hotloops wrapper script and document the tool.

Baremetal QEMU runner:
- Switch from user-mode to qemu-system-<arch> with -bios <elf>.
- Add --machine (default andes_ae350), --cpu (default
  andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024), --qemu-config (-readconfig),
  --cwd (chdir before launch so semihosting fread paths resolve), and
  --qemu-arg (repeatable passthrough).

RVV-only filter (--optimize-rvv, default on):
- Scan the ELF disassembly with objdump and drop loops whose
  [start_pc, end_pc] range contains no V-extension mnemonic (vsetvli,
  vle*, vse*, vadd*, ...). All detection lives in the script, so the
  TCG plugin remains unchanged. Use --no-optimize-rvv to disable.

LLM report mode (--llm, default on):
- Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption: header, TL;DR
  paragraph naming the hottest loop, and one per-loop fact-sheet block
  per reported edge with stable IDs (L1, L2, ...), pc_range, function,
  source file:line + inline code snippet, RVV instruction listing,
  parent/children loop IDs (inferred from PC-range containment), and
  direct callees (jal/jalr resolved via the <name> annotation). The
  TL;DR is templated from the data, no external call is made. Use
  --no-llm for the original table.

docs/hotloops.md:
- Describe the plugin, wrapper, both modes, output format, build
  prerequisites, and known limitations.

5c8ab568630890aafd4f366b373f23e8ffa90b77 contrib/plugins: add hotloops plugin for hot inner-loop detection
Detects loops by observing backward TB transitions: when the next
executed translation block starts at a PC <= the last instruction
PC of the previously executed TB, that pair (start_pc, end_pc) is
a loop edge whose iteration count we tally.

Plugin args: limit=N (top-N rows, default 50), min_iters=N (drop
loops below threshold). Output is sorted by iterations descending.

scripts/hotloops.sh wraps the plugin: takes a RISC-V ELF, auto-
detects rv32/rv64, runs qemu-<arch> with the plugin, then formats
the result as a table. Symbols are resolved via objdump and, when
the ELF has DWARF, source file:line is resolved via addr2line.

contrib/plugins: add hotloops tool for hot inner-loop detection

A TCG plugin plus a wrapper script and docs for finding hot inner
loops in RISC-V workloads.

Plugin (contrib/plugins/hotloops.c):
- Detects loops by observing backward TB transitions: when the next
  executed translation block starts at a PC <= the last instruction
  PC of the previously executed TB, that pair (start_pc, end_pc) is
  a loop edge whose iteration count we tally.
- Args: limit=N (top-N rows, default 50), min_iters=N (drop loops
  below threshold). Output is sorted by iterations descending.

Wrapper (scripts/hotloops.sh):
- Takes a RISC-V ELF, auto-detects rv32/rv64, runs the baremetal
  qemu-system-<arch> with -bios <elf> and the plugin, then formats the
  result. Symbols are resolved via objdump and, when the ELF carries
  DWARF, source file:line via addr2line.
- Baremetal knobs: --machine (default andes_ae350), --cpu (default
  andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024), --qemu-config (-readconfig),
  --cwd (chdir so semihosting fread paths resolve), and --qemu-arg
  (repeatable passthrough).
- RVV-only filter (--optimize-rvv, default on): scan the objdump
  disassembly and drop loops whose [start_pc, end_pc] range contains
  no V-extension mnemonic. Detection lives entirely in the script, so
  the plugin stays unchanged. --no-optimize-rvv disables it.
- LLM report mode (--llm, default on): emit a Markdown report with a
  TL;DR naming the hottest loop and one fact-sheet per loop (stable
  IDs, pc_range, function, source file:line + snippet, RVV listing,
  parent/child loop IDs, direct callees). --no-llm restores the table.

docs/hotloops.md documents the plugin, wrapper, both output modes,
build prerequisites, and known limitations.

  vill extracted from the MSB of the packed vtype representation.
- riscv_csrrw_check: skip the read-only gate when env->debugger is
  set (same flag already used for other debug-mode CSR overrides).

hw/riscv/andes_ae350: honor -object memory-backend-file for DRAM

Adopt the modern machine->ram idiom used by virt.c and most other QEMU
machines: set mc->default_ram_id and let the machine framework either
auto-create an anonymous memory-backend (the existing behavior) or
consume a user-supplied -object memory-backend-file,id=mem (the new
capability). Replace the local memory_region_init_ram(main_mem, ...)
+ add_subregion(..., main_mem) pair with a single add_subregion that
binds the DRAM range to machine->ram.

Behavior is unchanged for users who do not pass -object memory-backend:
the framework auto-creates an anonymous backend with the default_ram_id,
identical to the prior init_ram call. Users who pass
-machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem now get DRAM backed by a shared
file - required for the hybrid-sim QEMU<->vsim shared-RAM round-trip on
this board.

### 1. RVV detection lives in the bash script as disassembly text-scanning, not in the plugin — wrong altitude
**File:** `scripts/hotloops.sh` lines 161-186 (objdump capture), 303-325 (Python `is_rvv_mnemonic` / `has_rvv_in_range`); **doc** `docs/hotloops.md` 124-126.

In-tree precedent is `howvec.c`, which classifies vector instructions in-plugin by opcode mask/pattern.

**Why wrong altitude:** the plugin owns ground truth (the decoded stream QEMU actually executed); the script reconstructs a lossy text shadow of it via a *second, external* disassembler that may differ from QEMU's (llvm-objdump vs binutils vs the target gnu toolchain — the script picks whichever is on PATH, lines 148-149). **Deeper form:** have the plugin tag each TB (or each loop edge) with a `has_vector` bit computed once at translate time via `qemu_plugin_insn_data()` opcode test, gated on `info->target_name` being riscv. Emit it as an extra column in the raw output. The script then filters on a real bit and drops the entire second-objdump pass for the RVV path. But the *filter* decision (is this loop hot AND vector) is a property of execution, and that belongs in the plugin. **File:** `scripts/hotloops.sh` line 305: `return mn.startswith("v") and len(mn) > 1 and mn[1].isalpha()`.

This is a stringly-typed approximation of an opcode class. It is correct for *standard* RV mnemonics but has no defense against vendor/custom mnemonics, future extensions, or a different disassembler's naming. The codebase already encodes the precise RVV opcode pattern (`insn32.decode`), so a text prefix is strictly weaker than what's available.

A contrib tool's defaults should be either upstream-generic (e.g. `virt` + a baseline RVV cpu) or sourced from the environment, not a specific commercial SKU. **Deeper form:** default `MACHINE`/`CPU` from env vars (`HOTLOOPS_MACHINE`, `HOTLOOPS_CPU`) with an upstream-generic fallback, or document this as an Andes-specific wrapper and move it out of the contrib-styled `scripts/hotloops.sh` framing. **File:** `hotloops.c` 82-107 (`tb_start <= last_tail_pc`); **doc** 60-75.

The detector keys on `(current_tb_start, prev_tb_last_insn_pc)` and fires whenever a TB starts at `<=` the previous TB's last PC. The doc's "catches every loop... without modeling branch semantics" undersells that it also catches non-loops. Not a code change; a one-line doc honesty fix.

The `^v[a-z]` heuristic also silently misfits non-RISC-V targets (the script advertises `--arch riscv32|riscv64` only, but the plugin and machine are otherwise generic), and the doc itself has to add a caveat ("exact in practice") to defend it.

**Deeper form:** have the plugin tag each TB (or each loop edge) with a `has_vector` bit computed once at translate time via `qemu_plugin_insn_data()` opcode test, gated on `info->target_name` being riscv. Emit it as an extra column in the raw output. The script then filters on a real bit and drops the entire second-objdump pass for the RVV path. This also removes the on-PATH-objdump-must-agree-with-QEMU coupling.

Tradeoff worth stating: objdump is *still* needed for `--llm` mode's per-instruction operand listing and `<callee>` names (lines 327-343, 500-525), so the script cannot drop objdump entirely. But the *filter* decision (is this loop hot AND vector) is a property of execution, and that belongs in the plugin. Keeping operand-pretty-printing in the script is reasonable; keeping the hot/vector classification there is the bandaid.

### 2. RVV mnemonic test is a prefix-glob, not a decode — fragile even within the script's own altitude
**File:** `scripts/hotloops.sh` line 305: `return mn.startswith("v") and len(mn) > 1 and mn[1].isalpha()`.

This is a stringly-typed approximation of an opcode class. It is correct for *standard* RV mnemonics but has no defense against vendor/custom mnemonics, future extensions, or a different disassembler's naming. The codebase already encodes the precise RVV opcode pattern (`insn32.decode`), so a text prefix is strictly weaker than what's available.

**Deeper form:** same as finding 1 — classify by opcode, not by the first two characters of a disassembler's output string.

### 3. Hardcoded Andes machine/CPU defaults baked into a general-purpose contrib tool
**File:** `scripts/hotloops.sh` lines 57-58 (`MACHINE="andes_ae350"`, `CPU="andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024"`); **doc** 22-23, 32-33.

A `contrib/plugins` wrapper defaulting to a single vendor's downstream board + CPU is a project-local default wearing an upstream-tool costume. The plugin itself (`hotloops.c`) is correctly generic; the script pins it to Andes hardware.

**Why wrong altitude:** the defaults encode *this fork's* environment, not the tool's domain. A contrib tool's defaults should be either upstream-generic (e.g. `virt` + a baseline RVV cpu) or sourced from the environment, not a specific commercial SKU. It's defensible as a *team* convenience, but then it belongs alongside the team's other Andes-specific drivers (the repo already has `./hsim` and `scripts/` for that), not in `contrib/plugins/` styled as a generic detector.

**Deeper form:** default `MACHINE`/`CPU` from env vars (`HOTLOOPS_MACHINE`, `HOTLOOPS_CPU`) with an upstream-generic fallback, or document this as an Andes-specific wrapper and move it out of the contrib-styled `scripts/hotloops.sh` framing. The `--machine`/`--cpu`/`--cpu` flags already exist, so the override path is fine; only the hardcoded *default* is the issue.

### 4. Symbol/source resolution re-derived externally instead of using the plugin's symbol API — partial altitude miss
**File:** `scripts/hotloops.sh` lines 161-170 (objdump `-t` symbol table), 240-250 (Python `resolve`/`fn_of`); plugin emits only bare PCs (`hotloops.c` 152-154).

`qemu_plugin_insn_symbol()` exists and is used by `cflow.c`/`cache.c`. The plugin could attach the header/tail symbol to each edge directly. Instead the script parses objdump's symbol table with `awk` + `strtonum` and does a linear-scan address->FUNC mapping in Python (line 241, O(n) per lookup over an already-sorted list — `bisect` is imported and used elsewhere but not here).

**Why wrong altitude (weaker than #1):** unlike RVV class, symbolization is genuinely a post-processing concern and addr2line/DWARF source-line mapping legitimately needs the ELF on the host, so a script-side pass is reasonable. The miss is narrower: the *function-name* half is available in-plugin for free and would make `--raw` self-describing, and the manual symbol-table awk-munge (lines 163-170) duplicates what `qemu_plugin_insn_symbol()` already provides. I flag it as a should-consider, not a must-fix; the addr2line/source path is correctly script-side.

### 5. Loop "header/tail" model conflates distinct backward edges that share a target — depth limit, documented but worth noting
**File:** `hotloops.c` 82-107 (`tb_start <= last_tail_pc`); **doc** 60-75.

The detector keys on `(current_tb_start, prev_tb_last_insn_pc)` and fires whenever a TB starts at `<=` the previous TB's last PC. This is a deliberately shallow definition (the doc is honest about the `N` vs `N-1` count and same-function-only nesting). It is the right altitude *for a heuristic detector* and I am not asking for a CFG. One real consequence to surface: any backward control transfer counts — function returns to a lower-address caller, longjmp, and trap returns all register as "loops." The doc's "catches every loop... without modeling branch semantics" undersells that it also catches non-loops. Not a code change; a one-line doc honesty fix.

---

### Net
The plugin (`hotloops.c`) is at the right altitude and clean. The altitude problem is concentrated in the script: **the RVV classification (findings 1-2) is the material one** — it belongs in the plugin as an opcode-derived bit, and the current text-scan couples correctness to whichever external objdump is on PATH. Findings 3 (Andes hardcoding) and 4 (symbol API) are real but lower-severity; 5 is doc-only. None of the three files needs a rewrite; the deeper fix is to push the vector-ness bit down into the plugin and let the script keep only the genuinely-host-side work (operand pretty-print, DWARF source lines).

228	# --- symbols (FUNC syms): list of (addr, size, name) sorted by addr ---

310	    if not rvv_pcs or s > e:

316	    out = []

334	    i = bisect.bisect_left(disasm_pcs, s)

346	    """'path:42' or 'path:42 (discriminator 1)' -> (path, 42)."""

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hot inner-loop detector wrapper (system-mode, baremetal RISC-V).
#
# Runs a baremetal ELF under qemu-system-<arch> with the hotloops plugin
# and prints a sorted table of detected backward branches:
#
#   iters | start_pc -> end_pc | function:offset
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/hotloops.sh [opts] <elf>
#
# Options:
#   --arch <riscv32|riscv64|auto>   Target arch (default: auto)
#   --qemu <path>                   Override qemu-system binary
#   --plugin <path>                 Override plugin .so
#   --machine <name>                -M <name> (default andes_ae350)
#   --cpu <spec>                    -cpu <spec>
#                                   (default andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024)
#   --qemu-config <file>            -readconfig <file> (e.g. AE350 device cfg)
#   --cwd <dir>                     chdir before launching QEMU so semihosting
#                                   opens (fread of bin/*.bin) resolve
#   --qemu-arg <arg>                Append an extra arg to the QEMU command
#                                   (repeatable)
#   --limit <N>                     Top-N loops to print (default 50)
#   --min-iters <N>                 Drop loops with fewer than N iters (default 1)
#   --objdump <path>                Override objdump (resolves symbols)
#   --addr2line <path>              Override addr2line (resolves source lines)
#   --no-source                     Disable source file:line resolution
#   --raw                           Print raw plugin output, no formatting
#   --optimize-rvv                  Only report loops with at least one RVV
#                                   instruction (default: on)
#   --no-optimize-rvv               Disable the RVV-only filter
#   --llm                           Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM
#                                   consumption: TL;DR + per-loop fact-sheets
#                                   with stable IDs, source snippets, RVV
#                                   instruction listings, nesting, and direct
#                                   callees (default: on).
#   --no-llm                        Emit the plain human-readable table.
#   -h | --help                     Show help

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
QEMU_ROOT="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

ARCH="auto"
QEMU=""
PLUGIN=""
LIMIT=50
MIN_ITERS=1
OBJDUMP=""
ADDR2LINE=""
NO_SOURCE=0
RAW=0
OPTIMIZE_RVV=1
LLM=1
MACHINE="andes_ae350"
CPU="andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024"
QEMU_CONFIG=""
QEMU_CWD=""
EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS=()

usage() { sed -n '2,39p' "$0"; exit 0; }

# --- arg parsing ---
ELF=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --arch)        ARCH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --qemu)        QEMU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --plugin)      PLUGIN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --machine)     MACHINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --cpu)         CPU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --qemu-config) QEMU_CONFIG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --cwd)         QEMU_CWD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --qemu-arg)    EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
        --limit)       LIMIT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --min-iters)   MIN_ITERS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --objdump)     OBJDUMP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --addr2line)   ADDR2LINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --no-source)   NO_SOURCE=1; shift ;;
        --raw)         RAW=1; shift ;;
        --optimize-rvv)    OPTIMIZE_RVV=1; shift ;;
        --no-optimize-rvv) OPTIMIZE_RVV=0; shift ;;
        --llm)             LLM=1; shift ;;
        --no-llm)          LLM=0; shift ;;
        -h|--help)     usage ;;
        -*) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        *)
            if [[ -z "$ELF" ]]; then
                ELF="$1"; shift
            else
                echo "error: unexpected positional arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
            fi ;;
    esac
done

[[ -n "$ELF" ]] || { echo "error: ELF path required" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$ELF" ]] || { echo "error: not found: $ELF" >&2; exit 2; }

# --- arch detection ---
if [[ "$ARCH" == "auto" ]]; then
    file_out="$(file -L -- "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$file_out" in
        *"ELF 64-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv64 ;;
        *"ELF 32-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv32 ;;
        *) echo "error: cannot auto-detect arch (not RISC-V?), pass --arch" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
fi

# --- locate qemu + plugin ---
if [[ -z "$QEMU" ]]; then
    QEMU="${QEMU_ROOT}/build/qemu-system-${ARCH}"
fi
[[ -x "$QEMU" ]] || { echo "error: qemu not found/executable: $QEMU" >&2; exit 2; }

if [[ -z "$PLUGIN" ]]; then
    PLUGIN="${QEMU_ROOT}/build/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so"
fi
[[ -f "$PLUGIN" ]] || { echo "error: plugin not built: $PLUGIN" >&2; exit 2; }

# --- run ---
LOG="$(mktemp -t hotloops.XXXXXX.log)"
trap 'rm -f "$LOG"' EXIT

QEMU_CMD=("$QEMU"
          -plugin "${PLUGIN},limit=${LIMIT},min_iters=${MIN_ITERS}"
          -d plugin -D "$LOG"
          -M "$MACHINE"
          -cpu "$CPU"
          -nographic -semihosting
          -bios "$ELF")
[[ -n "$QEMU_CONFIG" ]] && QEMU_CMD+=(-readconfig "$QEMU_CONFIG")
[[ ${#EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ]] && QEMU_CMD+=("${EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]}")
if [[ -n "$QEMU_CWD" ]]; then
    ( cd "$QEMU_CWD" && "${QEMU_CMD[@]}" ) >/dev/null
else
    "${QEMU_CMD[@]}" >/dev/null
fi

if [[ "$RAW" -eq 1 ]]; then
    cat "$LOG"
    exit 0
fi

# --- symbol table from objdump (best effort) ---
if [[ -z "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
    for cand in llvm-objdump riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump \
                riscv32-unknown-elf-objdump objdump; do
        if command -v "$cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            OBJDUMP="$cand"
            break
        fi
    done
fi

SYMS="$(mktemp -t hotloops_syms.XXXXXX)"
LINES="$(mktemp -t hotloops_lines.XXXXXX)"
DISASM="$(mktemp -t hotloops_disasm.XXXXXX)"
trap 'rm -f "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM"' EXIT
if [[ -n "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
    # Capture FUNC symbols: addr size type name
    "$OBJDUMP" -t "$ELF" 2>/dev/null \
        | awk 'tolower($0) ~ /[ \t]f[ \t]/ && NF>=5 {
                  addr=strtonum("0x" $1);
                  size=strtonum("0x" $(NF-1));
                  name=$NF;
                  if (size>0) print addr, size, name;
              }' \
        | sort -n -k1,1 > "$SYMS" || true

    # Capture disassembly: each output line is "<hex-pc> <mnemonic> <operands>".
    # Works for both GNU binutils objdump and llvm-objdump. Used by the RVV
    # filter (mnemonic) and --llm mode (operands, callee names).
    if [[ "$OPTIMIZE_RVV" -eq 1 || "$LLM" -eq 1 ]]; then
        "$OBJDUMP" -d --no-show-raw-insn "$ELF" 2>/dev/null \
            | awk '
                /^[ \t]*[0-9a-fA-F]+:[ \t]+[^ \t]+/ {
                    line = $0;
                    sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line);
                    sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", line);
                    sub(/:[ \t]+/, " ", line);
                    print line;
                }' > "$DISASM" || true
    fi
fi

# --- locate addr2line for source line resolution (DWARF) ---
if [[ "$NO_SOURCE" -eq 0 && -z "$ADDR2LINE" ]]; then
    for cand in llvm-addr2line addr2line \
                riscv64-unknown-elf-addr2line riscv32-unknown-elf-addr2line \
                riscv64-linux-gnu-addr2line; do
        if command -v "$cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            ADDR2LINE="$cand"
            break
        fi
    done
fi

# Pre-collect all PCs from the log and batch-resolve to file:line.
# LINES file format: <hex-pc> <file:line>
if [[ "$NO_SOURCE" -eq 0 && -n "$ADDR2LINE" ]]; then
    pcs="$(awk -F',' '/^0x/ {gsub(/[ \t]/,"",$1); gsub(/[ \t]/,"",$2); print $1; print $2}' "$LOG" | sort -u)"
    if [[ -n "$pcs" ]]; then
        # addr2line: -e <elf> reads addrs on stdin, prints file:line.
        # We keep full paths here (no -s) so --llm mode can locate the
        # source file for code snippets; table mode basenames in Python.
        out="$(printf '%s\n' $pcs | "$ADDR2LINE" -e "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        paste <(printf '%s\n' $pcs) <(printf '%s\n' "$out") > "$LINES" || true
    fi
fi

# --- format ---
python3 - "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM" "$LIMIT" "$MIN_ITERS" \
        "$OPTIMIZE_RVV" "$LLM" "$ELF" <<'PY'
import sys, os, re, bisect

log_path     = sys.argv[1]
syms_path    = sys.argv[2]
lines_path   = sys.argv[3]
disasm_path  = sys.argv[4]
limit        = int(sys.argv[5])
min_iters    = int(sys.argv[6])
optimize_rvv = int(sys.argv[7]) == 1
llm_mode     = int(sys.argv[8]) == 1
elf_path     = sys.argv[9]

# --- symbols (FUNC syms): list of (addr, size, name) sorted by addr ---
syms = []
try:
    with open(syms_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 3:
                syms.append((int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]),
                             " ".join(parts[2:])))
except FileNotFoundError:
    pass

def resolve(pc):
    for addr, size, name in syms:
        if addr <= pc < addr + size:
            return f"{name}+0x{pc-addr:x}"
    return "?"

def fn_of(pc):
    for addr, size, name in syms:
        if addr <= pc < addr + size:
            return name
    return None

# --- source map: pc -> "path:line" (full path; basename in Python for table) ---
src_map = {}
try:
    with open(lines_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1)
            if len(parts) == 2:
                pc_str, src = parts
                src = src.strip()
                if src and not src.startswith("??"):
                    try:
                        src_map[int(pc_str, 16)] = src
                    except ValueError:
                        pass
except FileNotFoundError:
    pass

def src_full(pc):
    return src_map.get(pc, "")

def src_basename(s):
    """Basename the path part of a 'path:line[ (extra)]' string."""
    if not s:
        return ""
    head, sep, tail = s.partition(" ")
    return os.path.basename(head) + (sep + tail if sep else "")

def src_short(pc):
    return src_basename(src_full(pc))

# --- disassembly: pc -> (mnemonic, operands) ---
disasm = {}
try:
    with open(disasm_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.rstrip("\n")
            parts = line.split(None, 2)
            if len(parts) < 2:
                continue
            try:
                pc = int(parts[0], 16)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            mnemonic = parts[1]
            operands = parts[2] if len(parts) >= 3 else ""
            disasm[pc] = (mnemonic, operands)
except FileNotFoundError:
    pass

disasm_pcs = sorted(disasm.keys())

def is_rvv_mnemonic(mn):
    mn = mn.lower()
    return mn.startswith("v") and len(mn) > 1 and mn[1].isalpha()

rvv_pcs = sorted(pc for pc, (mn, _) in disasm.items() if is_rvv_mnemonic(mn))

def has_rvv_in_range(s, e):
    if not rvv_pcs or s > e:
        return False
    i = bisect.bisect_left(rvv_pcs, s)
    return i < len(rvv_pcs) and rvv_pcs[i] <= e

def rvv_insns_in_range(s, e):
    out = []
    if not rvv_pcs or s > e:
        return out
    i = bisect.bisect_left(rvv_pcs, s)
    while i < len(rvv_pcs) and rvv_pcs[i] <= e:
        pc = rvv_pcs[i]
        mn, ops = disasm[pc]
        out.append((pc, mn, ops))
        i += 1
    return out

CALL_MN = {"jal", "jalr", "c.jal", "c.jalr"}
CALLEE_RE = re.compile(r"<([^>]+)>")

def calls_in_range(s, e):
    out = []
    if not disasm_pcs or s > e:
        return out
    i = bisect.bisect_left(disasm_pcs, s)
    while i < len(disasm_pcs) and disasm_pcs[i] <= e:
        pc = disasm_pcs[i]
        mn, ops = disasm[pc]
        if mn in CALL_MN:
            m = CALLEE_RE.search(ops)
            target = m.group(1) if m else "(indirect)"
            out.append((pc, mn, target))
        i += 1
    return out

def parse_file_line(s):
    """'path:42' or 'path:42 (discriminator 1)' -> (path, 42)."""
    if not s or s.startswith("??"):
        return None, None
    m = re.match(r"^(.+?):(\d+)(?::\d+)?(?:\s|$)", s)
    if not m:
        return None, None
    return m.group(1), int(m.group(2))

def read_source_line(path, lineno):
    if not path or not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None
    try:
        with open(path, errors="replace") as f:
            for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
                if i == lineno:
                    return line.rstrip()
    except OSError:
        return None
    return None

# --- raw rows from plugin ---
rows = []
with open(log_path) as f:
    for line in f:
        m = re.match(r"\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)\s*,\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)\s*,\s*(\d+)",
                     line)
        if m:
            rows.append((int(m.group(1), 16),
                         int(m.group(2), 16),
                         int(m.group(3))))

if not rows:
    sys.stderr.write("hotloops: no backward edges observed\n")
    sys.exit(0)

total_iters_all = sum(r[2] for r in rows)

rows = [r for r in rows if r[2] >= min_iters]
if optimize_rvv:
    rows = [r for r in rows if has_rvv_in_range(r[0], r[1])]
rows.sort(key=lambda r: -r[2])
rows = rows[:limit]

if not rows:
    msg = f"hotloops: no loops with iters >= {min_iters}"
    if optimize_rvv:
        msg += " containing RVV instructions"
    sys.stderr.write(msg + "\n")
    sys.exit(0)

# --- Loop objects + nesting (PC-range containment) ---
class Loop:
    __slots__ = ("id", "start", "end", "iters", "parent", "children")
    def __init__(self, idx, s, e, c):
        self.id = f"L{idx}"
        self.start = s
        self.end = e
        self.iters = c
        self.parent = None
        self.children = []

loops = [Loop(i + 1, s, e, c) for i, (s, e, c) in enumerate(rows)]

for loop in loops:
    best = None
    best_size = None
    for cand in loops:
        if cand is loop:
            continue
        if cand.start <= loop.start and loop.end <= cand.end:
            if cand.start == loop.start and cand.end == loop.end:
                continue  # identical range, ambiguous - skip
            sz = cand.end - cand.start
            if best is None or sz < best_size:
                best = cand
                best_size = sz
    loop.parent = best

for loop in loops:
    if loop.parent is not None:
        loop.parent.children.append(loop)

# ============================================================
# --- LLM mode: Markdown report with TL;DR + per-loop blocks ---
# ============================================================
if llm_mode:
    def pct(n):
        return (100.0 * n / total_iters_all) if total_iters_all else 0.0

    def render_tldr(top):
        rvv_list = rvv_insns_in_range(top.start, top.end)
        if rvv_list:
            uniq = []
            seen = set()
            for _, mn, _ in rvv_list:
                if mn not in seen:
                    seen.add(mn)
                    uniq.append(mn)
            rvv_str = "RVV (" + ", ".join(uniq[:3])
            if len(uniq) > 3:
                rvv_str += f", +{len(uniq) - 3} more"
            rvv_str += ")"
        else:
            rvv_str = "scalar"
        fn = fn_of(top.start) or "?"
        src_s = src_short(top.start) or "?"
        if top.parent is None:
            nest_str = "top-level (no parent loop)"
        else:
            nest_str = f"nested inside {top.parent.id}"
        if top.children:
            cs = ", ".join(c.id for c in top.children)
            child_str = (f"and contains {len(top.children)} inner loop(s): "
                         f"{cs}")
        else:
            child_str = "and contains no inner loop"
        return (f"Hottest loop is {top.id} in `{fn}` ({src_s}), "
                f"{top.iters} iters = {pct(top.iters):.1f}% of total. "
                f"Body is {rvv_str}. It is {nest_str}, {child_str}.")

    print("# Hotloops Report")
    print(f"target:           {os.path.basename(elf_path)}")
    print(f"total_iters:      {total_iters_all}")
    print(f"reported_loops:   {len(loops)}")
    print(f"min_iters:        {min_iters}")
    print(f"rvv_filter:       {'on' if optimize_rvv else 'off'}")
    print()
    print("## TL;DR")
    print(render_tldr(loops[0]))
    print()
    print("## Loops")
    for idx, loop in enumerate(loops):
        tag = " [hottest]" if idx == 0 else ""
        print()
        print(f"### {loop.id}{tag}  ({pct(loop.iters):.1f}% of total)")
        print(f"iters:        {loop.iters}")
        size = loop.end - loop.start
        print(f"pc_range:     0x{loop.start:x} .. 0x{loop.end:x}  "
              f"(size: {size} B)")
        print(f"function:     {resolve(loop.start)} -> {resolve(loop.end)}")
        src_s = src_full(loop.start)
        src_e = src_full(loop.end)
        if src_s and src_e and src_s == src_e:
            print(f"source:       {src_basename(src_s)}")
        else:
            print(f"source:       {src_basename(src_s) or '?'}"
                  f" -> {src_basename(src_e) or '?'}")
        path, lineno = parse_file_line(src_s)
        snippet = read_source_line(path, lineno) if path and lineno else None
        if snippet:
            snippet = snippet.strip()
            if len(snippet) > 200:
                snippet = snippet[:197] + "..."
            print(f"code:         {snippet}")
        rvv_list = rvv_insns_in_range(loop.start, loop.end)
        if rvv_list:
            print(f"rvv:          yes ({len(rvv_list)} insn"
                  f"{'s' if len(rvv_list) != 1 else ''})")
            print(f"rvv_insns:")
            for pc, mn, ops in rvv_list[:8]:
                print(f"  - 0x{pc:x}  {mn:<10s} {ops}")
            if len(rvv_list) > 8:
                print(f"  - ... ({len(rvv_list) - 8} more)")
        else:
            print(f"rvv:          no")
        print(f"parent:       {loop.parent.id if loop.parent else '-'}")
        if loop.children:
            cs = ", ".join(c.id for c in loop.children)
            print(f"children:     [{cs}]")
        else:
            print(f"children:     []")
        callees = calls_in_range(loop.start, loop.end)
        if callees:
            print(f"calls:")
            for pc, mn, target in callees[:8]:
                print(f"  - 0x{pc:x}  {mn} -> {target}")
            if len(callees) > 8:
                print(f"  - ... ({len(callees) - 8} more)")
        else:
            print(f"calls:        []")
    sys.exit(0)

# ============================================================
# --- table mode (default, human-readable) ---
# ============================================================
hdr = f"# hot loops (iters >= {min_iters}"
if optimize_rvv:
    hdr += ", RVV-only"
hdr += f"), sorted desc, top {len(rows)}"
print(hdr)

have_src = bool(src_map)

w_iter = max(len("iters"), max(len(str(r[2])) for r in rows))
w_pc = 18  # 0x + 16 hex
w_sym = max(len("location"),
            max(len(f"{resolve(r[0])} -> {resolve(r[1])}") for r in rows))

if have_src:
    def srcpair(s, e):
        a, b = src_short(s), src_short(e)
        if a and b and a == b:
            return a
        return f"{a or '?'} -> {b or '?'}"
    w_src = max(len("source"),
                max(len(srcpair(r[0], r[1])) for r in rows))
    print(f"{'iters':>{w_iter}} | {'start_pc':<{w_pc}} -> "
          f"{'end_pc':<{w_pc}} | {'location':<{w_sym}} | source")
    print("-" * (w_iter + 3 + w_pc + 4 + w_pc + 3 + w_sym + 3 + w_src))
    for s, e, c in rows:
        loc = f"{resolve(s)} -> {resolve(e)}"
        print(f"{c:>{w_iter}} | 0x{s:016x} -> 0x{e:016x} | "
              f"{loc:<{w_sym}} | {srcpair(s, e)}")
else:
    print(f"{'iters':>{w_iter}} | {'start_pc':<{w_pc}} -> "
          f"{'end_pc':<{w_pc}} | location")
    print("-" * (w_iter + 3 + w_pc + 4 + w_pc + 3 + w_sym))
    for s, e, c in rows:

        print(f"{c:>{w_iter}} | 0x{s:016x} -> 0x{e:016x} | {loc}")

- File/line: `target/riscv/csr.c:876-892` (`write_vtype`), mirroring `read_vtype` at `csr.c:835-851`.
- Summary: `write_vtype` switches on `env->xl` and hardcodes the vill bit position as `1u << 31` (RV32) / `1ULL << 63` (RV64). The canonical unpack already exists in `HELPER(vsetvl)` at `target/riscv/vector_helper.c:44-45`:
  ```c
  int xlen = riscv_cpu_xlen(env);
  bool vill = (s2 >> (xlen - 1)) & 0x1;
  ```
  `riscv_cpu_xlen()` (`target/riscv/cpu.h:777`, `return 16 << env->xl`) collapses the whole `switch (env->xl)` into one width expression.
- Duplication cost: the new switch is a third copy of the same xl->MSB mapping (read_vtype, vsetvl, now write_vtype). Each adds an `MXL_RV128`/future-mode `g_assert_not_reached()` arm that vsetvl's branch-free form avoids. The two magic shift constants must stay in sync with read_vtype by hand.
- Reuse: call `riscv_cpu_xlen(env)`. The body becomes branch-free, e.g.
  ```c
  int xlen = riscv_cpu_xlen(env);
  env->vill  = (val >> (xlen - 1)) & 1;
  env->vtype = val & ~((target_ulong)1 << (xlen - 1));
  ```
  Note this also fixes a latent narrowing bug in the diff: on RV32, `~(target_ulong)(1u << 31)` is computed in 32-bit then widened, so on an RV64 build (`target_ulong` = 64-bit) the high 32 bits of the mask are 0 and `~` of a 32-bit value gets zero-extended — the clear-mask is wrong. - File/line: `target/riscv/csr.c:879` (`switch (env->xl)`).
- Summary: you asked whether an xl->width helper exists.
